title: Yellowed Molten German Potato Hash
description: A salty, molten German dish featuring lime juice and fried potatoes, perfect for a sick day, made low-glycemic-friendly and served in an agave leaf vessel.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large bowl, toss the diced potatoes with olive oil, salt, black pepper, and paprika until they are evenly coated.
Spread the potatoes out in a single layer on a baking sheet and roast for 20 minutes, or until they are golden brown.
While the potatoes are roasting, heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and add the diced onion, cooking until it is translucent and starting to caramelize.
Add the minced garlic to the skillet and cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
Once the potatoes are done roasting, add them to the skillet with the onion and garlic, and stir to combine.
Squeeze the freshly squeezed lime juice over the top of the potato mixture and stir to combine.
Reduce heat to low and simmer the mixture for an additional 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes are crispy and golden brown.
To serve, scoop the potato mixture into the center of an agave leaf, and serve hot.
